note: Editorial operationalization of the intervention distinction attributed to Tomicah in the user-supplied notes. These are proposed, potentially complementary mechanisms, not findings that any named provider is captured or that a legal power already exists.

nodes.title: Web protocols and standards
nodes.market: Pool procurement around independently implementable interfaces and verifiable conformance.
nodes.policy: Apply lawful public-procurement and interoperability requirements where an authorized body can do so.
nodes.nonMarket: Funded standards participation, open deliberation, shared maintenance, and minority appeal routes.
nodes.philanthropic: Seed independent reference implementations, accessibility participation, and public-interest technical capacity.

nodes.title: Browser and agent
nodes.market: Use member-authorized purchasing and credible routing or supplier exit.
nodes.policy: Enforce applicable consumer, privacy, disclosure, and portability duties.
nodes.nonMarket: Share reviewed configurations, accessible guidance, and accountable user representation.
nodes.philanthropic: Support early usability, isolation tests, migration tools, and inclusion subsidies.

nodes.title: Domain and application
nodes.market: Combine recurring demand and authorized contributions in transparent service agreements.
nodes.policy: Review platform terms and competitive coordination under the applicable legal framework.
nodes.nonMarket: Member and supplier governance, published criteria, and independent complaints.
nodes.philanthropic: Bootstrap catalogs, outreach, rights review, and participation before recurring demand exists.

nodes.title: CDN and edge
nodes.market: Negotiate pooled service, log, blocking-review, and funded exit commitments.
nodes.policy: Use applicable communications, privacy, and review obligations; do not invent control over a provider.
nodes.nonMarket: Maintain shared operations knowledge and permission-safe failover exercises.
nodes.philanthropic: Fund independent testing, migration readiness, and smaller operators' technical support.

nodes.title: Identity and permission
nodes.market: Procure compatible identity and privacy services without selling blanket permission.
nodes.policy: Establish lawful processing bases and preserve applicable individual and third-party protections.
nodes.nonMarket: Rights stewardship, comprehensible mandates, and reusable refusal and appeal procedures.
nodes.philanthropic: Support accessible consent design, alternative authentication, and independent rights expertise.

nodes.title: Database, server, and cloud
nodes.market: Buy hosting with usable export, bounded exit costs, and verified service continuity.
nodes.policy: Review processing, confidentiality, retention, and migration obligations in the relevant jurisdictions.
nodes.nonMarket: Shared schemas, stewardship protocols, and collective maintenance.
nodes.philanthropic: Seed export tools, independent data review, and underfunded maintenance capacity.

nodes.title: Model and compute
nodes.market: Compare eligible suppliers and negotiate valuable, authorized updates or contributor services.
nodes.policy: Assess applicable rights and deployment duties; evaluate any new outcome or participation requirement separately.
nodes.nonMarket: Maintain shared evaluations, alternatives, and plural public-interest objectives.
nodes.philanthropic: Fund open benchmarks, bounded pilots, and participation where buyers alone will not finance them.

nodes.title: Provenance, quality, and validation
nodes.market: Sell independent assurance, integration, freshness, or delivery services, not favorable scores.
nodes.policy: Require truthful claims and usable challenge under applicable law; no automatic certification from registry entry.
nodes.nonMarket: Maintain an open core of methods, versions, limitations, and contestable summaries.
nodes.philanthropic: Support baseline evaluation access, independent reviewers, and trustworthy public discovery.

nodes.title: Payment and settlement
nodes.market: Contract for transparent regulated payment services and agreed benefit allocations.
nodes.policy: Resolve payments, tax, consumer-protection, safeguarding, and unclaimed-fund duties.
nodes.nonMarket: Participatory budgeting, independent reconciliation, and protected member liabilities.
nodes.philanthropic: Seed ledger infrastructure, complaint capacity, and clearly disclosed participation support.

nodes.title: Community and energy return
nodes.market: Negotiate lawful procurement and community-benefit commitments with accountable operators.
nodes.policy: Use authorized utility, environmental, siting, and public cost-allocation processes.
nodes.nonMarket: Community organizing, deliberation, independent monitoring, and public-interest advocacy.
nodes.philanthropic: Fund independent engineering and representation without buying consent or offsetting unrelated local harms.
